focus: Frontier node F-1-006: traceability, closing the checklist_evidence core protocol

findingDetails.title: The packet's last completion criterion understates the phase count
findingDetails.scopeProof: listed the packet directory and counted eleven 0*/ phase folders; read goal.md:93 verbatim; the criterion names no glob and no explicit folder list, so its scope is fixed by the numeral alone
findingDetails.case: an operator runs the criterion's command, sees RESULT: PASSED, and records the packet as validated while phases 007 to 011 were never in the validated set
findingDetails.claim: The packet's sixth completion criterion validates six phases while the packet holds eleven, so its PASS cannot cover the packet it names.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: checked whether --recursive on the packet folder would reach every child regardless of the numeral: it would, so the numeral is descriptive rather than operative. That reading makes the criterion's command correct and its wording wrong, which is still a traceability defect because the wording is what a reader checks the result against. Checked whether a later phase records the eleven-folder run: no phase records a recursive run after 006.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: the numeral may be a leftover from the packet's original six-phase shape that nobody re-read after 007 was added. That is the same defect stated as a cause rather than a refutation.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: drop if the criterion is reworded to name the packet folder alone, or to name all eleven phases, which makes the wording match what the command validates
